question: Will North Korea launch at least one ballistic missile between September 3 and September 5, 2026?
resolution_criterion: This question resolves YES if South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff (JCS) reports, or [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) report citing South Korean, US, or Japanese military/government officials, that North Korea launched at least one ballistic missile at any time between 00:00 September 3, 2026 and 23:59 September 5, 2026, Korea Standard Time (UTC+9). A single launch event involving multiple missiles counts. It resolves NO if no such ballistic-missile launch during that window is reported. A later report confirming a launch that occurred within the window still counts.
reference_class: 3-day calendar windows in 2026 containing >=1 JCS-reported DPRK ballistic-missile launch event (~12 events / 246 days)
reasoning:
[pooled 3 independent runs [0.07, 0.06, 0.08] -> 0.070; the narrative below is the research run's own view (0.07)]
Reference class: JCS-counted DPRK ballistic-missile launch EVENTS in 2026 — ~11 by Aug 12 per South Korean assessment, plus the Aug 20 salvo, i.e. ~12 over 246 days = ~0.049/day; a random 3-day window contains one ~14% of the time. But the window is not random and not fresh: 00:00 Sep 3 KST -> 23:59 Sep 5 KST is 42.8% elapsed as of Now, with no launch reported in searches through Sep 3, so only ~41.2h remain (Poisson tail ~6-8%). Regime is a quiet post-exercise stretch: Ulchi Freedom Shield ended Aug 27 and the last reported event was Aug 20; launches cluster around drills and anniversaries, and the Sep 9 founding anniversary sits outside the window, so short-window hazard is if anything below the annual average. Counterweight: 2026 tempo is high, launches are unannounced and can come any morning, and my index coverage of Sep 3 KST evening is imperfect, so a small residual for an already-occurred-but-unindexed launch. Thin, one-sided evidence (absence of news) keeps me near the base-rate-implied tail rather than far below it.
what_would_change_my_mind: A JCS/NHK/Japan MoD report of a launch (or attempted launch) dated 3-5 Sep 2026 KST — resolves YES immediately
Navigation warnings, NOTAMs, or KCNA/Kim Jong Un site-visit signalling pointing to an imminent test
A new US-ROK exercise, a ROK/US strategic-asset deployment, or a DPRK statement threatening 'corresponding action' inside the window
Evidence the Aug 20-Sep 3 lull was punctuated by an event I missed (i.e. the true 2026 event count/hazard is higher than 12/246)

question: Will SpaceX's Starship Flight 14 (Ship 41) reach orbit between September 3 and September 5, 2026?
resolution_criterion: This question resolves YES if the Starship upper stage designated Ship 41, flying on SpaceX's Starship Flight 14 (also referred to as Integrated Flight Test 14), lifts off from Starbase, Texas between 00:00 UTC on September 3, 2026 and 23:59 UTC on September 5, 2026 AND achieves orbit, meaning it completes at least one full revolution around the Earth (a sustained low Earth orbit, as opposed to the suborbital/transatmospheric trajectories of Flights 1-13). Resolution will be based on the entry for Flight 14 (Ship 41) in the "List of Starship launches" Wikipedia page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Starship_launches): the question resolves YES if that entry records the Ship's orbit as "Low Earth orbit" (or an equivalent orbital, non-suborbital classification) for a launch dated within the window, and NO otherwise. If Wikipedia does not clearly reflect the outcome, official SpaceX statements or [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) will be used.
reference_class: Announced-but-undated SpaceX Starship integrated flight tests, evaluated over 3-day windows more than a week before the operator's own filed operations date and with no launch road closure posted
reasoning:
[pooled 3 independent runs [0.01, 0.01, 0.01] -> 0.008; the narrative below is the research run's own view (0.01)]
Resolution needs a conjunction: liftoff inside a ~50-hour remaining window AND a successful first-ever orbital insertion. Every schedule instrument points past the window: SpaceX's own FCC STA (signed 2026-08-21) gives a start-of-operations date of 2026-09-15; the COMPASS manifest slide reads NET 2026-09-15; several launch trackers carry NET 2026-09-30. Wikipedia's flight-14 article says only 'NET early September 2026' with no announced date. Starbase/Cameron County have posted no launch road closure for Sept 3-5 — only overnight road *delays* on Sep 3-4, the signature of ground testing/transport, not a launch; launch closures are normally posted 2-5 days ahead as a signed mayoral order, and none exists. Hardware is close (B21 33-engine static fire Aug 28, S41 six-engine 60s static fire Aug 21), but no full-stack rollout, WDR, or FAA license-modification approval has been reported. Base rate for 'launch occurs inside a 3-day window when no date is announced, no closure is filed, and the operator's own filing names a date 10+ days later' is near zero; I hold ~1.5% for the liftoff leg and ~0.7 conditional for orbital insertion on a first attempt. No human market matching this contract exists (Polymarket's space section carries only a 2026 launch-count market, wrong contract), so no anchor is applied.
what_would_change_my_mind: Cameron County / City of Starbase posting a primary launch road closure for Sept 4 or Sept 5
SpaceX publishing a launch webcast page or Musk/SpaceX announcing a Sept 3-5 launch time
FAA issuing the Flight 14 license modification plus a full-stack rollout and WDR completed on Sept 3
An amended FCC STA moving the start-of-operations date earlier than Sept 15

missing_evidence: No confirmation of FAA license-modification status for Flight 14, and no explanation for the Sept 15 (filing) vs Sept 30 (tracker) discrepancy; neither is load-bearing since both dates sit after the window.

No confirmation either way of a full-stack rollout/WDR in the last 24h, and no Cameron County closure page read after 2026-09-03; the Sep 15 (FCC/COMPASS) vs Sep 30 (trackers) discrepancy remains unexplained.

question: Will Sony announce a new PlayStation State of Play showcase between September 3 and September 5, 2026?
resolution_criterion: This question resolves YES if, at any time from 00:00 UTC on September 3, 2026 through 23:59 UTC on September 5, 2026, Sony Interactive Entertainment officially announces a new "State of Play" broadcast (a livestreamed PlayStation showcase presenting game news and trailers), as posted on the official PlayStation.Blog (https://blog.playstation.com/) or reported by [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions). The announcement counts regardless of when the broadcast itself is scheduled to air. Otherwise it resolves NO.
reference_class: 3-day calendar windows containing a first-time official Sony announcement of a new State of Play broadcast, 2019-2026 (~5-6 such announcement days per year), further conditioned on the window's immediate aftermath of a just-aired State of Play
reasoning:
[pooled 3 independent runs [0.06, 0.03, 0.04] -> 0.042; the narrative below is the research run's own view (0.06)]
The September 2026 State of Play (plus the back-to-back State of Play Japan) was officially announced by Sony on Monday, August 31, 2026 — three days BEFORE the question's window opens. The fine print explicitly excludes re-shares/re-promotion of a State of Play announced before Sept 3, so the flood of Sept 2-3 coverage does not satisfy the criterion. The broadcasts themselves aired Sept 3 at 13:00 UTC and have already concluded (~9h before Now); blog.playstation.com as of Now carries only reveal posts and an 'all announcements' recap, no announcement of a further, future State of Play. YES therefore requires Sony to announce an entirely NEW, not-previously-announced State of Play in the ~50h remaining — hours after having just run two shows back-to-back. Sony's announcement cadence is ~5-6 State of Play announcements per year with gaps of many weeks; an unconditional 2.1-day window gives ~3.5%, and conditioning on 'a show aired this morning' pushes the genuine-event rate to roughly 1%. No prediction market (Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold, bookmakers) prices this question — searched, none found. The bulk of my probability is therefore resolver risk on a near-miss: a resolver skimming Sept 3-dated headlines reading 'Sony announces State of Play' could resolve YES against the fine print.
what_would_change_my_mind: A PlayStation.Blog post or official PlayStation social post dated Sept 3-5, 2026 announcing a further, previously unannounced State of Play (e.g. a game-specific deep-dive or a Tokyo Game Show tie-in show)
Evidence that the State of Play Japan broadcast was in fact first announced on Sept 3, separately from the Aug 31 announcement, rather than in the same Aug 31 post
A statement inside the Sept 3 broadcast (which I have only recap coverage of, not a full transcript) teasing a dated future State of Play
Resolver precedent on this question series showing pre-window announcements being counted from in-window news coverage

missing_evidence: No transcript or closing-slate detail of the Sept 3 broadcasts was available — only journalist recaps — so a brief on-air tease of a future State of Play cannot be fully ruled out; no prediction market (Polymarket/Kalshi/Manifold/bookmakers) prices this event.

No full transcript/closing-slate of the Sept 3 broadcasts was available — only journalist recaps; a brief end-of-show tease could in principle have gone unreported, though that is unlikely across a dozen recaps.

question: Will the M/V LUTUF and its crew be freed from pirate control before September 5, 2026?
resolution_criterion: This question resolves YES if the M/V LUTUF — the Cameroon-flagged cargo vessel hijacked on 17 August 2026 off Puntland, Somalia — and its crew are confirmed to have been freed from the control of the hijackers before 23:59 UTC on September 4, 2026. "Freed" means the crew (or the surviving/remaining crew) is confirmed to be no longer under the physical control of the hijackers, whether by negotiated release, naval/military rescue, escape, or the hijackers abandoning the vessel and crew. It resolves NO if, as of 23:59 UTC on September 4, 2026, no such confirmation has occurred and the vessel and/or crew remain under hijacker control (this is the default). Resolution is based on official statements from EU NAVFOR Operation ATALANTA (https://eunavfor.eu/news) or reporting from [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions).
reference_class: Somali pirate hijackings of merchant vessels, 2024-2026 wave, resolved (crew freed) within ~19 days of seizure
reasoning:
[pooled 3 independent runs [0.97, 0.97, 0.97] -> 0.970; the narrative below is the research run's own view (0.97)]
Reference class (Somali hijackings resolved within ~19 days of seizure) implies a low prior, roughly 20-25% — most cases run months. That prior is superseded by direct evidence: multiple independent credible outlets (AP via Al Jazeera/WTOP, gCaptain, DefenceWeb, Splash247, Hiiraan, Somali Guardian, Rio Times) reported on 29-30 August 2026 that the M/V LUTUF and its 10 crew were freed. Somalia's federal Defence Ministry attributes this to a 10-day joint Somali-Turkish naval operation (4 pirate boats destroyed, 14 pirates killed); Puntland's Ministry of Security denies any military operation and says the pirates left voluntarily after a ransom of roughly $2.5m was paid. The two accounts conflict on mechanism but agree on the fact of release, and the criterion accepts negotiated release, military rescue, escape, or hijackers abandoning the vessel alike. Question is therefore effectively already resolved five days before the 4 Sep cutoff. Residual NO paths: a strict resolver requiring EU NAVFOR ATALANTA confirmation (ATALANTA does not appear to have issued its own liberation notice, this being a non-EU operation), an unreported re-capture before 23:59 UTC 4 Sep, or ambiguity from a 2 Sep TV5MONDE piece citing six vessels still held at end-August without clarifying whether LUTUF is counted. Each is small; several outlets note no government has formally confirmed crew condition, which is a confirmation-quality caveat rather than evidence of continued captivity.
what_would_change_my_mind: A credible report (UKMTO, EU NAVFOR ATALANTA, or the owner Polar Movement Shipping) that the crew remain aboard under hijacker control or were re-taken
An ATALANTA or UKMTO advisory still listing LUTUF among vessels currently held as of 3-4 September 2026
Reporting that only the vessel was recovered while crew were taken ashore as hostages

missing_evidence: ['No official crew-condition or crew-location statement from the flag state, Polar Movement Shipping, the Indian MEA, or UKMTO dated after 30 Aug 2026', 'No ATALANTA newsroom item on LUTUF either way']

No post-30 Aug statement from the flag state, owner Polar Movement Shipping, the Indian MEA, or UKMTO explicitly confirming the 10 crew's whereabouts; no prediction market (Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold) prices this event — none found, so no crowd anchor was used.

question: Will Ethereum's closing price exceed $2,500 on September 4, 2026?
resolution_criterion: This question resolves YES if the daily closing price of Ethereum (ETH) in US dollars for September 4, 2026 (UTC) is greater than $2,500.00, as reported on CoinGecko's Ethereum price history page: https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/ethereum/historical_data (the "Close" value for the row dated 2026-09-04). Otherwise it resolves NO. For example, a close of $2,501.34 resolves YES; a close of $2,499.99 or $2,500.00 resolves NO.
reference_class: One-day-ahead binary crypto-close contracts where spot sits within +/-1% of the strike at ~26h to expiry (near-ATM), cross-checked against the narrower class of ETH daily UTC closes above $2,500 during the Aug 21-Sep 3 2026 range
reasoning:
[pooled 3 independent runs [0.53, 0.47, 0.52] -> 0.507; the narrative below is the research run's own view (0.53)]
Live spot is $2,508-2,511 (CoinGecko API 21:25Z, Coinbase), i.e. ~0.4% ABOVE the $2,500 strike, with ~26h until the 2026-09-05T00:00Z measurement of the Sept 4 UTC close. Realized daily SD from CoinGecko's own 14-day UTC-midnight series is ~3.0% (2.1% ex-outlier); ETH IV implies ~3.4%/day. A lognormal random walk from S=$2,511 with sigma_26h=3.5% gives P(close>2500)=~0.55, and the answer is nearly sigma-invariant (0.54-0.56 for sigma 3-4%) because the question is essentially at-the-money. Shaded down ~2pts: the move is a short-squeeze leg (~$265M shorts liquidated, ETF inflows) that has stalled at $2,500-2,522, and $2,500-2,515 has been the ceiling of a two-week $2,380-2,515 range in which only 3 of 14 daily prints closed above $2,500, each retracing within 1-2 days. Counterweight: crypto one-day autocorrelation is ~zero, so range-resistance is weak evidence (n=3). No human market prices this contract; Kalshi's ETH dailies had no liquidity near the strike and use a different index and expiry. Live macro two-sided (US strikes on Iran, oil >$96) adds variance without direction.
what_would_change_my_mind: ETH trading below ~$2,460 or above ~$2,570 during Sept 4 UTC — each ~2.5% move away from the strike shifts this by roughly 20 points
A discrete catalyst in the window: a large spot-ETF flow print (a second consecutive outflow day, or another $200M+ inflow day), or a US macro release moving risk assets
Escalation or de-escalation in the Iran situation / a sharp oil move, which has been driving crypto risk-off this week
Discovery of a liquid prediction market whose contract actually matches (>$2,500, Sept 4 UTC daily close, CoinGecko) pricing materially away from ~50%
Evidence that CoinGecko's historical_data 'Close' for date D is the 00:00Z snapshot of D rather than D+1 — that would collapse the horizon to ~2h and push this well above 0.6

question: Will U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs record a single-day net inflow exceeding $500 million on any trading day between August 31 and September 7, 2026?
resolution_criterion: This question resolves YES if, on any U.S. equity trading day from August 31, 2026 through September 4, 2026 (inclusive), the aggregate net flow across all U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs is greater than +$500 million (i.e. a value above 500.0 in the "Total" row, expressed in US$m), as reported in the Bitcoin ETF Flow table at https://farside.co.uk/btc/ . For example, a "Total" of 606.3 for a given date resolves YES; a "Total" of 307.5 does not. Otherwise it resolves NO. (September 7, 2026 is Labor Day, when U.S. equity markets and these ETFs do not trade, so no flows occur on that date.)
reference_class: Single US equity trading days in 2026 in which the aggregate net flow across all US spot bitcoin ETFs (Farside 'Total' row) exceeded +$500m
reasoning:
[pooled 3 independent runs [0.15, 0.12, 0.15] -> 0.139; the narrative below is the research run's own view (0.15)]
Five eligible flow days (Aug 31, Sep 1-4); three are already published and all far below the bar: +216.7, -236.5, +101.1 (US$m, Farside/TFTC). Only the Sep 3 print (session closed, data not yet out as of 2026-09-03T22:14Z) and Sep 4 remain. Reference class: single-day aggregate flows in 2026, where +$500m days are rare — Aug 19's +517.2 was reported as the largest since early May, i.e. ~0 in roughly 75 trading days, and August (the best month of 2026 at +$3.52bn) produced only 2 of 21 sessions above the threshold. Since Aug 20 the max daily print is +337.6. Bullish update: BTC jumped ~5.5% to ~$81.5k on Sep 3 (Waller rate-pause signal + Middle East de-escalation), and creations often lag a mid-session macro rally by a day, so both remaining prints sit above the unconditional rate. Counterargument: September flows have been choppy with an outflow day, IBIT's best recent day was only ~$205m, and even the far stronger August rally week cleared $500m on just 2 of 5 sessions. Two shots at a ~5-10% conditional daily event, positively correlated, lands in the mid-teens.
what_would_change_my_mind: The Sep 3 Farside/SoSoValue print publishing above roughly +$400m, which would show creations catching up to the price rally and make Sep 4 a live second shot
A published Sep 3 print in the usual +$50-250m band, which would leave only Sep 4 and push this toward single digits
BTC giving back the Sep 3 rally intraday on Sep 4 (or a hot NFP/yield shock), historically coincident with flat-to-negative flow days
Reporting of an unusually large single-ticket IBIT creation or a model-portfolio allocation event, the mechanism behind most >$500m prints
